AX8052 ERRATA

LPOSC Calibration Should Not Be Used                            · Wakeup Timer (WTCFGA, WTCFGB)
  The built-in automatic LPOSC calibration logic can
                                                                   For setting WTCFGx to value y, use the following code
cause LPOSC output glitches when enabled, and should               sequence:
therefore not be used.
                                                                     1. WTCFGx |= 0x04;
  Setting LPOSCKFILT to a value significantly lower than             2. WTCFGx = 0x0F;
the maximum kFILT value given in the programming manual              3. WTCFGx &= y | 0xFC;
(such as 100th of the maximum kFILT value) will limit the            4. WTCFGx = y;
frequency and the effect on the tuning word of the glitches.
However, occasional glitches will still occur and propagate     · ADC (ADCCLKSRC)
to the LPOSC consumers. The application must be able to
tolerate the occasional LPOSC glitch (eg. if a timer is driven     Only switch ADC clock sources while all
by LPOSC, it may occasionally increment twice per LPOSC            ADCCHxCONFIG registers are set to 0xFF
period).
                                                                · SPI Master (SPSCKSRC)
  Workaround: Enable LPOSC calibration, but set
LPOSCKFILT to zero. When an LPOSC Calibration                      Only switch SPI Master clock sources while SPMODE
interrupt is signaled (see register OSCCALIB), read the            is not set to SPI Master, i.e. SPMODE  01
period register (LPOSCPER) and manually compute the
new LPOSC tuning word. Delay writing the computed               · Timer (TxCLKSRC)
tuning word to LPOSCFREQ until approximately 1/4th of
the LPOSC period after the LPOSC Calibration interrupt             Only switch Timer clock sources while TxMODE is set
was signaled.                                                      to Off, i.e. TxMODE = 000

Changing Clock Sources May Accidentally Enable XOSC or            It is recommended to add seven NOP instructions
LPXOSC                                                          immediately after the write instruction that sets PCON bits
                                                                1:0 to 01, or alternatively to use the libmf function
  Changing the clock source of any peripheral may               enter_sleep() to prevent this current spike.
accidentally enable the Crystal Oscillator or the Low Power
Crystal Oscillator.                                             Affected Revisions: V1
                                                                Fixed in Revision: V1C, V2
  If crystals are connected to PA0/PA1 and PA3/PA4 and
these pins are configured as analog inputs, the oscillators     CPU Clock Rates Less than 10 kHz Not Recommended
will switch off again after two falling clock cycles, and         ON Semiconductor does not recommend to run the
therefore this is not a problem.
                                                                Microcontroller Core at less than 10 kHz (less than 10000
  Otherwise, these oscillators may be switched off again        Instructions/s). Instead, the Microcontroller should be run
manually by calling libmf routines turn_off_xosc() and          from a faster clock source, and be put in standby or sleep
turn_off_lpxosc(). These routines require to toggle             mode when the system is idle.
PA0/PA1 and PA3/PA4, respectively.
                                                                Affected Revisions: V1
  The accidental enabling of the Crystal Oscillators may be     Fixed in Revision: V1C, V2
avoided by carefully switching clock sources as follows:

· System Clock (CLKCON)

    Only switch to and from any clock source via
      FRCOSC

    When switching from FRCOSC to LPXOSC, first
      switch to LPOSC, then to LPXOSC.
      When switching from LPXOSC to FRCOSC, first
      switch to LPOSC, then FRCOSC.

Temperature Sensor Should Be Converted with the CPU in         Power-On Reset
Standby Mode                                                     A power-up voltage ramp start voltage of 0.3 V or less is

  When converting the temperature sensor value, the CPU        required for V1 silicon to reliably signal power-on Reset.
should be set to Standby mode. Otherwise, the converted        For V1C, a start voltage of 0.6 V or less is required.
temperature values will be noisier and the average will be
affected as well. Wake-up from Standby mode can be               Starting with revision V2 the POR generation circuitry is
effected either by an ADC interrupt handler, or using the      fully level sensitive, triggering POR at a VDD_IO level of
code sequence below:                                           typically 1 V and insensitive to the ramp start voltage or
                                                               speed.
  start conversion (see ADCCONV register)                      Affected Revisions: V1, V1C
     for (;;) {                                                Fixed in Revision: V2
               EA = 0;
               if (ADCCONV & 0x80)                             RESET_N during VDDIO Ramp-Up
                                           break;                If the external RESET_N input is asserted (held low)
               EIE_6 = 1;
               enter_standby();                                during VDDIO Voltage Ramp-Up, an elevated current draw
               EIE_6 = 0;                                      may be observed on VDDIO. As soon as RESET_N is
               EA = 1;                                         deasserted, the current returns to normal levels. Subsequent
     }                                                         assertions of RESET_N while VDDIO remains supplied
     EA = 1;                                                   will not cause any elevated current draw. This additional
     read ADCCH0VAL0                                           current will not damage the chip, it is however
     read ADCCH0VAL1                                           recommended to keep RESET_N pulses short.

  The ADC clock source (register ADCCLKSRC) should             Affected Revisions: V1, V1C
be set to the same clock as the system clock (register         Fixed in Revision: V2
CLKCON). The divider should be set so that the conversion
rate falls into the range given by the datasheet. The ADC      Timer TXIRQRO, TXIRQRU, TXIRQEO , TXIRQEU Clear on
clock source should not be set to system clock (register       Read takes Precedence over Set
ADCCLKSRC(2:0) should not be set to 110), because the
system clock is turned off during standby. Most commonly,        The timer status bits TxIRQRO , TxIRQRU, TxIRQEO ,
the microcontroller runs from the internal fast RC oscillator  TxIRQEU are designed to clear on read. Clearing on read
(CLKCON = 0x00), in this case the recommended ADC              takes precedence in the affected chips. So software polling
clock setting for temperature conversion is                    the status bits in a tight loop miss overflow or underflow
ADCCLKSRC = 0x30.                                              events whenever the event coincides with reading the status

                                                               GPADC Missing Codes
                                                                 The GPADC converter exhibits missing codes at

                                                               mid-level (or zero in differential mode) input.

                                                               Affected Revisions: V1, V1C, V2
